  "text": "The station clock had stopped at twenty past four, but Mr Bell still checked it before unlocking his shoe-repair shop.

“You could get a watch,” said Nina, who sold flowers opposite.

“I know what time it is.”

“Then why look?”

He bent to lift the shutter.

In March, the railway announced that the old shops would be replaced with ticket machines. Nina found another pitch outside the hospital. Mr Bell put a handwritten notice in his window: ALL REPAIRS TO BE COLLECTED BY FRIDAY.

On Thursday evening, one pair remained. Small brown boots, newly soled, with a yellow bead threaded onto one lace.

He rang the number on the ticket. It was no longer connected.

“Leave them with lost property,” Nina said.

He wrapped the boots in paper.

For three weeks, they sat beneath her flower stall. Then she moved them onto a shelf behind the buckets, away from the rain.

In May, a woman stopped to buy carnations. Her daughter stood beside her in sandals, though the morning was cold.

Nina noticed a yellow bead hanging from the zip of the child’s coat.

“Did you leave some boots at the station?”

The woman lowered the flowers.

“We had to move rather quickly.”

Nina fetched the parcel.

“How much do I owe?”

“There’s a ticket inside.”

The woman unfolded it. Beneath the price, Mr Bell had written a telephone number.

“He’s working from home now,” Nina said.

The child sat on an upturned crate to try the boots. Her mother held the carnations while Nina loosened the laces.

They were a little tight. Nina fetched a shoehorn, and the child pushed her heel down."
